source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Chapter 6 (PDF 143-169, printed 140-166); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 6 (Bioenergetics), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.
Bioenergetics and ATP: the energy currency of cells

blocks.prompt: 1 The study of how energy flows through living systems is called:
blocks.explanation: Bioenergetics is the study of how energy flows through living systems, i.e. how cells store and expend energy.

book_ref.quote: Bioenergetics is the study of how energy flows through living systems

blocks.prompt: 2 Which pair correctly matches the two processes with their roles in bioenergetics?

options.text: Photosynthesis captures energy; respiration releases energy
Photosynthesis releases energy; respiration captures energy

blocks.explanation: Photosynthesis acts as an energy-capturing process while respiration acts as an energy-releasing process.

book_ref.quote: Photosynthesis acts as an energy–capturing while respiration as an energy-releasing process

blocks.prompt: 3 Nearly all the energy used by living organisms on Earth comes from:
blocks.explanation: Plants, algae and certain bacteria capture sunlight and convert it into chemical energy; this forms the base of the food chain.

book_ref.quote: Nearly all the energy used by living organisms on Earth comes from photosynthesis

blocks.text: ATP: The Energy Currency of Cells

blocks.prompt: 4 Chemically, the energy currency of the cell (ATP) is a:
blocks.explanation: The cell's energy currency is a nucleotide called adenosine triphosphate (ATP).

book_ref.quote: This currency is actually a nucleotide called adenosine triphosphate (ATP)

blocks.prompt: 5 The sugar present in a molecule of ATP is:
blocks.explanation: ATP has three subunits: adenine (a nitrogen containing base), ribose (a five-carbon sugar) and three phosphate groups.

book_ref.quote: ribose (a five-carbon sugar) and three phosphate groups

blocks.prompt: 6 ATP was discovered in 1929 by:
blocks.explanation: Karl Lohmann discovered ATP in 1929; in 1941 Fritz Lipmann proposed that ATP is the main energy-transfer molecule.

book_ref.quote: ATP was discovered in 1929 by Karl Lohmann

blocks.prompt: 7 Who proposed in 1941 that ATP is the main energy-transfer molecule in the cell?
blocks.explanation: The Nobel prize winner Fritz Lipmann proposed this in 1941.

book_ref.quote: Fritz Lipmann proposed that ATP is the main energy-transfer molecule in the cell

blocks.prompt: 8 Breaking one high-energy phosphate bond of ATP releases about:
blocks.explanation: About 7.3 kcal (7,300 calories) per mole of ATP is released when one phosphate bond is broken.

book_ref.quote: The breaking of one phosphate bond releases about 7.3 kcal (7,300 calories) per mole of ATP

blocks.prompt: 9 In common energy reactions, when only the outer P-P high-energy bond of ATP breaks, ATP becomes:
blocks.explanation: Only the outer P-P bond breaks, so ATP becomes ADP (adenosine diphosphate) and one Pi is released.

book_ref.quote: In common energy reactions only the outer P-P high-energy bond breaks

blocks.prompt: 10 In some cases ADP is further broken down to:
blocks.explanation: ADP + H₂O → AMP + Pi + energy (7.3 kcal/mole).

book_ref.quote: In some cases, ADP is further broken down to AMP (adenosine monophosphate) and Pi:

blocks.prompt: 11 ATP is made during ____ processes and broken down during ____ processes.
blocks.explanation: Cells store energy from oxidation of food by joining ADP and Pi; ATP is broken in energy-consuming processes. So ATP transfers energy between reactions.

book_ref.quote: ATP is made during energy-releasing processes and it is broken down during energy-consuming processes

blocks.prompt: 12 Why does water appear on both sides of the summary equation of photosynthesis?

options.text: It is only a solvent and takes no part
It is produced only by respiration
It is the main product of photosynthesis
It is used as a reactant in some reactions and released as a product in others

blocks.explanation: Water is used in some reactions and released in others; there is no net yield of water.

book_ref.quote: Water appears on both sides of the equation because water is used as reactant in some reactions

blocks.prompt: 13 In the summary equation of photosynthesis, the products are:
blocks.explanation: CO₂, water and light are the reactants; glucose and oxygen are the products: 6CO₂ + 12H₂O + light → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ + 6H₂O.

book_ref.quote: Carbon dioxide, water and light are the reactants while glucose and oxygen are the products

blocks.prompt: 14 The moment when there is no net gas exchange between leaves and atmosphere because photosynthesis and respiration are equal is called:
blocks.explanation: At dawn and dusk, when light intensity is low, the two rates may be equal for a short time: this is the compensation point.

book_ref.quote: This is termed as compensation point

blocks.prompt: 15 The compensation point is usually reached:
blocks.explanation: At dawn and dusk the light intensity is low, so photosynthesis and respiration may be equal for a short time.

book_ref.quote: At dawn and dusk, when light intensity is low, the rate of photosynthesis and respiration may be equal

blocks.prompt: 16 At noon, when light intensity is high, the leaves show:

options.text: net release of carbon dioxide and uptake of oxygen
net release of oxygen and uptake of carbon dioxide

blocks.explanation: At noon photosynthesis is faster; respiration cannot supply enough CO₂ and more O₂ is made than respiring cells need.

book_ref.quote: So, the result is the net release of oxygen coupled with the uptake of carbon dioxide

blocks.prompt: 17 During photosynthesis, the hydrogen used for the reduction of CO₂ comes from:
blocks.explanation: Water is the source of hydrogen for the reduction of CO₂.

book_ref.quote: Water is the source of hydrogen, for the reduction of CO₂ during photosynthesis

blocks.prompt: 18 In the 1930s, who hypothesized that plants split water as a source of hydrogen, releasing oxygen as a by-product?
blocks.explanation: The hypothesis was given by C. B. van Niel (the book prints 'Van Neil'); it was confirmed in the 1940s.

book_ref.quote: In 1930s, Van Neil hypothesized that plant splits water as a source of hydrogen

blocks.prompt: 19 Which isotopic tracer was used to confirm that the oxygen of photosynthesis comes from water?
blocks.explanation: Scientists prepared H₂¹⁸O and C¹⁸O₂ using the heavy-oxygen isotope ¹⁸O.

book_ref.quote: An experiment was conducted in which isotopic tracer (¹⁸O) of oxygen was used

blocks.prompt: 20 Plants given H₂¹⁸O and normal CO₂ released:
blocks.explanation: The first group (H₂¹⁸O + C¹⁶O₂) produced ¹⁸O, showing the released oxygen comes from water.

book_ref.quote: It was found that plants of first group produced ¹⁸O but the plants of second group produced normal oxygen

blocks.prompt: 21 The 'reducing power' for the reduction of CO₂ to sugar is:
blocks.explanation: Hydrogen from water reduces NADP to NADPH, which serves as the reducing power for the reduction of CO₂.

book_ref.quote: This hydrogen reduces the coenzyme nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADP) to NADPH

blocks.prompt: 22 Photosynthetic pigments are present in:
blocks.explanation: Photosynthetic pigments are present in thylakoid membranes and capture light energy.

book_ref.quote: Photosynthetic pigments are present in thylakoid membranes

blocks.prompt: 23 Light behaves like a stream of particles called:
blocks.explanation: Light behaves like a stream of particles called photons; pigment molecules absorb one photon at a time.

book_ref.quote: Light behaves like a stream of particles called photons

blocks.prompt: 24 Compared with red photons, blue photons have:
blocks.explanation: Short wavelength (blue) photons have higher energy than long wavelength (red) photons.

book_ref.quote: Short wavelength photons (blue) have a higher energy than long wavelength (red) photons

blocks.prompt: 25 Chlorophylls found in photosynthetic bacteria are known as:
blocks.explanation: Chlorophyll a, b, c and d are found in plants and algae; others found in photosynthetic bacteria are bacteriochlorophylls.

book_ref.quote: while the others are found in photosynthetic bacteria and are known as bacteriochlorophylls

blocks.prompt: 26 The four pyrrole rings of the porphyrin ring of chlorophyll are held together by a central atom of:
blocks.explanation: The four pyrrole rings are held together by a magnesium atom in the centre.

book_ref.quote: The four pyrrole rings are held together by a magnesium atom in the centre

blocks.prompt: 27 Which part of the chlorophyll molecule anchors it in the thylakoid membrane?
blocks.explanation: The hydrophobic tail is a long hydrocarbon chain that anchors the molecule; the porphyrin head absorbs light.

book_ref.quote: The tail is made of long hydrocarbon chain. It anchors the molecule in the thylakoid membrane

blocks.prompt: 28 Which wavelengths are least absorbed by chlorophylls?
blocks.explanation: Chlorophylls absorb mainly violet-blue and orange-red; green is least absorbed and is transmitted or reflected.

book_ref.quote: Green wavelengths are least absorbed by chlorophylls and are transmitted or reflected

blocks.prompt: 29 Besides capturing light, carotenoids such as beta-carotene also:

options.text: protect the photosynthetic apparatus from damage by excess light

blocks.explanation: Carotenoids capture light in the blue and green regions and protect the photosynthetic apparatus from excess light.

book_ref.quote: Carotenoids, such as beta-carotene, play dual role in photosynthesis

blocks.prompt: 30 Phycobilins are accessory pigments found in:
blocks.explanation: Chlorophyll b and carotenoids are found in plants, while phycobilins are found in red algae and cyanobacteria.

book_ref.quote: phycobilins are found in the red algae and cyanobacteria

blocks.prompt: 31 Which of these is NOT an accessory pigment?
blocks.explanation: Accessory pigments are all pigments other than chlorophyll a that can gather light for photosynthesis.

book_ref.quote: Accessory pigments include all the pigments, other than chlorophyll-a

blocks.prompt: 32 The generally believed order of energy transfer among pigments in plants is:
blocks.explanation: Accessory pigments pass their energy towards chlorophyll a: carotenoids → chlorophyll b → chlorophyll a.

book_ref.quote: It is generally believed that the order of transfer of energy in plants is;

blocks.prompt: 33 The absorption spectrum of chlorophylls shows maximum absorption at about:
blocks.explanation: Maximum absorption is of blue light (430 nm) and red light (670 nm).

book_ref.quote: Absorption spectrum of chlorophylls indicates that absorption of blue light (430 nm) and red light (670 nm) is maximum

blocks.prompt: 34 Some wavelengths not absorbed by chlorophyll a are absorbed well by chlorophyll b and vice versa. This:

options.text: increases the range of light absorbed
makes chlorophyll b the reaction-centre pigment

blocks.explanation: Such differences increase the range of light absorbed by both chlorophylls.

book_ref.quote: Such differences increase the range of light absorbed by both chlorophylls

blocks.prompt: 35 About what percentage of the solar energy received do plants convert into chemical energy?
blocks.explanation: Plants convert only about 1-2% of the solar energy they receive; this is still enough to sustain almost all life.

book_ref.quote: Plants convert only about 1-2% of the solar energy they receive into chemical energy

blocks.prompt: 36 The light energy converted into chemical energy is stored in organic compounds in the form of:
blocks.explanation: Absorbed light energy is converted to chemical energy stored as C-H bond energy.

book_ref.quote: stored in organic compounds in the form of C-H bond energy

blocks.prompt: 37 The first action spectrum was made in 1883 by:
blocks.explanation: The German biologist T. W. Engelmann made the first action spectrum in 1883.

book_ref.quote: The first action spectrum was made by a German biologist, T. W. Engelmann in 1883

blocks.prompt: 38 Engelmann made the first action spectrum using the alga:
blocks.explanation: He worked on the photosynthetic pigments of Spirogyra.

book_ref.quote: He worked on the photosynthetic pigments of Spirogyra

blocks.prompt: 39 While making an action spectrum, the rate of photosynthesis is measured by the amount of:
blocks.explanation: A plant is lit with different colours one by one and the oxygen emitted from leaves is measured for each colour.

book_ref.quote: the rate of photosynthesis is measured by measuring the amount of oxygen emitted from leaves

blocks.prompt: 40 In Engelmann's experiment, maximum oxygen was emitted from the Spirogyra cells receiving:
blocks.explanation: Maximum photosynthesis occurred in cells receiving blue and red light, so maximum oxygen came from these cells.

book_ref.quote: maximum photosynthesis occurred in the cells which received blue and red spectrum of light

blocks.prompt: 41 In photosynthesis, CO₂ acts as the source of:
blocks.explanation: Sugar is formed by reduction of CO₂ using ATP and NADPH; CO₂ is the carbon source.

book_ref.quote: In this way, CO₂ acts as the source of carbon for making sugars

blocks.prompt: 42 The entry of CO₂ into the leaves depends upon:
blocks.explanation: CO₂ enters through stomata and dissolves in water of mesophyll cell walls; entry depends on stomatal opening.

book_ref.quote: The entry of CO₂ into the leaves is dependent upon the opening of stomata

blocks.prompt: 43 Aquatic photosynthetic organisms use as their carbon source:

options.text: dissolved CO₂, bicarbonates and soluble carbonates

blocks.explanation: Aquatic organisms use dissolved CO₂, bicarbonates and soluble carbonates; land organisms use atmospheric CO₂.

book_ref.quote: Aquatic photosynthetic organisms use dissolved CO₂, bicarbonates and soluble carbonates as carbon source

blocks.prompt: 44 Clusters of photosynthetic pigments embedded in thylakoid membranes are called:
blocks.explanation: For efficient absorption and use of solar energy, pigments are organized into clusters called photosystems.

book_ref.quote: photosynthetic pigments are organized into clusters, called photosystems

blocks.prompt: 45 Each photosystem consists of:

options.text: an antenna complex and a reaction centre

blocks.explanation: Each photosystem has a light-gathering antenna complex and a reaction centre.

book_ref.quote: Each photosystem consists of a light gathering ‘antenna complex’ and a ‘reaction centre’

blocks.prompt: 46 The reaction centre of a photosystem has one or more molecules of:
blocks.explanation: The reaction centre has chlorophyll a, which passes high-energy electrons to a primary electron acceptor.

book_ref.quote: The reaction centre has one or more molecules of chlorophyll-a

blocks.prompt: 47 Photosystem-I and photosystem-II are named so in order of their:
blocks.explanation: The two photosystems are named in order of their discovery.

book_ref.quote: These are named so in order of their discovery

blocks.prompt: 48 The reaction centre of PS-I has:
blocks.explanation: PS-I has P700 chlorophyll a, absorbing maximum light of 700 nm; PS-II has P680 (680 nm).

book_ref.quote: PS-I has P700 chlorophyll-a molecule in its reaction centre

blocks.prompt: 49 The light-dependent reactions take place:

options.text: on the thylakoid membranes of the grana

blocks.explanation: Light-dependent reactions occur on thylakoid membranes of the grana; light-independent reactions occur in the stroma.

book_ref.quote: The light-dependent reactions take place on the thylakoid membranes of the grana

blocks.prompt: 50 The formation of ATP in the light-dependent reactions is called:
blocks.explanation: Formation of ATP, the most important step of light-dependent reactions, is called photophosphorylation.

book_ref.quote: The formation of ATP is the most important step of light-dependent reactions

blocks.prompt: 51 In non-cyclic photophosphorylation:

options.text: both PS-I and PS-II take part

blocks.explanation: In the non-cyclic pathway both photosystems participate and two electron chains are involved.

book_ref.quote: In non-cyclic pathway, both photosystems i.e., PS-I and PS-II participate

blocks.prompt: 52 After losing its excited electrons, P680 chlorophyll becomes:
blocks.explanation: An electron 'hole' is created in P680, which becomes a strong oxidizing agent.

book_ref.quote: an electron “hole” is created in p680 chlorophyll, which has become a strong oxidizing agent

blocks.prompt: 53 The water-splitting step of photosynthesis is called:
blocks.explanation: Water reacting with oxidized chlorophyll of PS-II breaks into 2H⁺, an oxygen atom and two electrons: photolysis.

book_ref.quote: This water splitting step of photosynthesis is called photolysis

blocks.prompt: 54 The main source of atmospheric oxygen is the oxygen produced during:
blocks.explanation: The oxygen produced during photolysis is the main source of atmospheric oxygen.

book_ref.quote: The oxygen produced during photolysis is the main source of atmospheric oxygen

blocks.prompt: 55 The electron transport chain between PS-II and PS-I consists of:

options.text: coenzyme Q, cytochrome b and cytochrome c

blocks.explanation: The chain of PS-II has plastoquinone (PQ), cytochrome complex and plastocyanin (PC).

book_ref.quote: This chain consists of electron carriers called plastoquinone (PQ), cytochrome complex, and plastocyanin (PC)

blocks.prompt: 56 In the second electron transport chain, the photoexcited electrons from PS-I are first received by:
blocks.explanation: The primary acceptor of PS-I passes electrons to the second chain, where ferredoxin (FD) receives them.

book_ref.quote: These electrons are received by ferredoxin (FD)

blocks.prompt: 57 The enzyme that transfers electrons from ferredoxin to NADP⁺ is:
blocks.explanation: NADP reductase transfers electrons from FD to NADP⁺, which with two electrons and an H⁺ becomes NADPH.

book_ref.quote: An enzyme NADP reductase transfers these electrons from FD to NADP⁺

blocks.prompt: 58 The zigzag path of electrons through PS-II, PS-I and the electron transport chains is called:
blocks.explanation: This zigzag path is the Z-scheme; it runs through PS-II and PS-I (the book misprints 'PS-II and PS-II').

book_ref.quote: The zigzag path taken by electrons through PS-II and PS-II and electron transport chains, is called Z-scheme

blocks.prompt: 59 Cyclic electron flow uses:
blocks.explanation: Cyclic electron flow uses PS-I but not PS-II; electrons cycle back to P700.

book_ref.quote: This path uses PS-I but not PS-II

blocks.prompt: 60 Cyclic photophosphorylation happens when:

options.text: the Calvin cycle slows down and NADPH accumulates

blocks.explanation: It happens when the Calvin cycle slows down and NADPH accumulates in the chloroplast; it gives ATP but no NADPH or O₂.

book_ref.quote: It happens when Calvin cycle slows down and NADPH accumulates in chloroplast

blocks.prompt: 61 In the chloroplast, the energy released from electrons is used to pump H⁺ ions:

options.text: from the lumen into the stroma
from the cytosol into the stroma
from the stroma into the thylakoid lumen
from the matrix into the inter-membrane space

blocks.explanation: The energy is spent on active transport of H⁺ from the stroma to the inner compartment (lumen).

book_ref.quote: this energy is spent for the active transport of H⁺ ions from the stroma of chloroplast to its inner compartment (lumen)

blocks.prompt: 62 The membrane protein through which H⁺ ions diffuse back and which joins ADP with Pi is:
blocks.explanation: ATP synthase uses the energy of the H⁺ flow to bond ADP with inorganic phosphate.

book_ref.quote: This protein is an enzyme called ATP synthase

blocks.prompt: 63 ATP is generated by chemiosmosis in:
blocks.explanation: The electron transport chains of mitochondria and chloroplasts make ATP by the same mechanism of chemiosmosis.

book_ref.quote: The electron transport chains in mitochondria and chloroplasts generate ATP by the same mechanism of chemiosmosis

blocks.prompt: 64 The light-independent reactions happen in the:
blocks.explanation: They happen in the stroma, using carbon from CO₂, energy from ATP and hydrogen from NADPH.

book_ref.quote: Light-independent reactions are a series of reactions which happen in the stroma of chloroplast

blocks.prompt: 65 The 'dark reactions' of photosynthesis can occur:

options.text: in light or darkness, as long as ATP and NADPH are available

blocks.explanation: They can occur in the absence as well as presence of light as long as ATP and NADPH are available.

book_ref.quote: These reactions can occur in the absence as well as in the presence of light

blocks.prompt: 66 Melvin Calvin was awarded the Nobel Prize for working out the dark reactions in:
blocks.explanation: The details were discovered by Melvin Calvin and colleagues at the University of California; Nobel Prize 1961.

book_ref.quote: Calvin was awarded Nobel Prize in 1961 for this work

blocks.prompt: 67 The enzyme that is probably the most abundant protein on Earth is:
blocks.explanation: Ribulose biphosphate carboxylase (rubisco) is probably the most abundant protein on Earth.

book_ref.quote: probably the most abundant protein on Earth

blocks.prompt: 68 The initial incorporation of CO₂ into organic material is called:
blocks.explanation: Carbon fixation is the first phase of the Calvin cycle: the initial incorporation of CO₂ into organic material.

book_ref.quote: Carbon fixation refers to the initial incorporation of CO₂ into organic material

blocks.prompt: 69 The Calvin cycle is also called the C-3 pathway because:

options.text: the first product of carbon fixation is a three-carbon compound
it uses three ATP molecules only

blocks.explanation: The product of initial carbon fixation (3-PGA) is a three-carbon compound.

book_ref.quote: Since the product of initial carbon fixation is a three–carbon compound

blocks.prompt: 70 In the reduction phase of the Calvin cycle, 1,3-biphosphoglyceric acid is reduced to:
blocks.explanation: Each 1,3-biphosphoglyceric acid is reduced to G3P; NADPH provides the hydrogen.

book_ref.quote: Each 1,3-biphsophoglyceric acid is then reduced to Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate (G3P)

blocks.prompt: 71 Of the six G3P molecules produced in the Calvin cycle, how many leave the cycle?
blocks.explanation: One G3P leaves the cycle (two such G3P make glucose); the other five regenerate RuBP.

book_ref.quote: In this way, six molecules of G3P are produced, out of which one molecule leaves the cycle

blocks.prompt: 72 In the regeneration phase, five molecules of G3P are converted into:
blocks.explanation: Five G3P form three RuP; then three ATP add a phosphate to each RuP to make three RuBP.

book_ref.quote: five molecules of G3P are converted into three molecules of Ribulose phosphate (RuP)

blocks.prompt: 73 The exchange of CO₂ and O₂ between an organism and its environment is called:
blocks.explanation: This exchange is external respiration or breathing; cellular respiration is the step-by-step oxidation of food in cells.

book_ref.quote: The exchange of CO₂ and O₂ between the organism and its environment is called external respiration or breathing

blocks.prompt: 74 Glucose has more stored energy than CO₂ and H₂O because glucose has:
blocks.explanation: There are many C-H bonds in glucose but no such bonds in CO₂ and H₂O.

book_ref.quote: The reason is that there are many C-H bonds in glucose

blocks.prompt: 75 Glucose is known as the respiratory fuel because:

options.text: it is the only sugar in cells
almost all cells in all organisms use it as energy source
it is made only in animals

blocks.explanation: Almost all cells in all organisms use glucose as energy source; hence glucose is the respiratory fuel.

book_ref.quote: That is why, glucose is known as respiratory fuel

blocks.prompt: 76 The molecular formula of pyruvic acid is:
blocks.explanation: In the first step of both types of respiration glucose splits into two pyruvic acid (C₃H₄O₃).

book_ref.quote: glucose is split into two molecules of pyruvic acid (C₃H₄O₃) in a process called glycolysis

blocks.prompt: 77 In anaerobic respiration one glucose molecule yields only:
blocks.explanation: Only two ATPs (about 2% of the energy of glucose), equivalent to 14.6 kcal.

book_ref.quote: one glucose molecule yields only two ATPs (only about 2% of the energy present in glucose)

blocks.prompt: 78 The energy in the two ATPs produced by anaerobic respiration of one glucose is equivalent to:
blocks.explanation: Each ATP bond gives about 7.3 kcal, and the two ATPs equal 14.6 kcal.

book_ref.quote: The energy in two ATPs is equivalent to 14.6 kcal

blocks.prompt: 79 Alcoholic fermentation of pyruvic acid occurs in:
blocks.explanation: Alcoholic fermentation occurs in primitive prokaryotes (bacteria) and some eukaryotes such as yeast.

book_ref.quote: In primitive prokaryotic cells (bacteria) and in some eukaryotic cells such as yeast

blocks.prompt: 80 Lactic acid fermentation occurs in human muscle cells:

options.text: during extreme physical activity when oxygen cannot be supplied fast enough

blocks.explanation: It happens during extreme physical activity, when oxygen cannot be transported to the cells as rapidly as needed.

book_ref.quote: This form of anaerobic respiration occurs in muscle cells of humans and other animals

blocks.prompt: 81 The molecular formula of lactic acid is:
blocks.explanation: Lactic acid is C₃H₆O₃ (book correction; the book prints C₂H₆O₃). Lactic acid fermentation releases no CO₂.

book_ref.quote: The formula of lactic acid is C₃H₆O₃, not C₂H₆O₃

blocks.prompt: 82 Aerobic respiration became possible on Earth after:

options.text: the evolution of fermentation in yeast
the loss of oxygen from the atmosphere
oxygen accumulated in the atmosphere through photosynthesis

blocks.explanation: Early life had no free O₂; photosynthesis slowly accumulated O₂, making aerobic respiration possible.

book_ref.quote: The presence of free oxygen made evolution of aerobic respiration possible

blocks.prompt: 83 Which stage of aerobic respiration takes place in the cytosol?
blocks.explanation: Glycolysis occurs in the cytosol without needing oxygen; the other three stages occur in mitochondria.

book_ref.quote: Glycolysis occurs in the cytosol and oxygen is not essential for this stage

blocks.prompt: 84 The first step of glycolysis converts glucose into:
blocks.explanation: A phosphate group is transferred from ATP to glucose, forming glucose 6-phosphate.

book_ref.quote: A phosphate group is transferred from ATP to glucose

blocks.prompt: 85 How many ATP molecules are spent in the preparatory phase of glycolysis (per glucose)?
blocks.explanation: One ATP phosphorylates glucose and another phosphorylates fructose 6-phosphate to fructose 1,6-biphosphate.

book_ref.quote: So, it becomes fructose 1, 6-biphosphate

blocks.prompt: 86 Fructose 1,6-biphosphate breaks into G3P and:
blocks.explanation: It breaks into two three-carbon intermediates, G3P and DAP, which inter-convert to give two G3P.

book_ref.quote: glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate (G3P) and dihydroxy acetone phosphate (DAP)

blocks.prompt: 87 In the oxidative phase of glycolysis, hydrogen removed from G3P is transferred to:
blocks.explanation: Two hydrogen atoms are removed from G3P and transferred to NAD⁺, and a Pi is added, giving 1,3-BPGA.

book_ref.quote: It results in a molecule of 1, 3-biphosphoglyceric acid (1,3-BPGA)

blocks.prompt: 88 2-phosphoglyceric acid is converted to phosphoenol pyruvic acid by:
blocks.explanation: 2-PGA is dehydrated (water removed) into PEP.

book_ref.quote: 2-PGA is dehydrated (water removed) into phosphoenol pyruvic acid (PEP)

blocks.prompt: 89 During pyruvic acid oxidation, removal of CO₂ from pyruvic acid forms:
blocks.explanation: Removal of CO₂ changes pyruvic acid to acetaldehyde, which is oxidized to an acetyl group that joins CoA.

book_ref.quote: A molecule of carbon dioxide is removed from pyruvic acid. So, it changes into acetaldehyde

blocks.prompt: 90 The citric acid cycle was largely worked out by the British biochemist:
blocks.explanation: Sir Hans Krebs worked out much of the cycle, so it is called the Krebs cycle.

book_ref.quote: Much of this cycle was worked out by a British biochemist, Sir Hans Krebs

blocks.prompt: 91 The Krebs cycle is also called the citric acid cycle because:

options.text: six-carbon citric acid is formed in its first step
citric acid is its final product
it occurs only in citrus fruits
it uses citric acid as coenzyme

blocks.explanation: It is named after the six-carbon citric acid formed in its first step.

book_ref.quote: after the six-carbon citric acid molecule formed in its first step

blocks.prompt: 92 In the first step of the Krebs cycle, the acetyl group combines with:
blocks.explanation: The acetyl group combines with four-carbon oxaloacetic acid to form six-carbon citric acid.

book_ref.quote: The acetyl group combines with a four-carbon molecule, oxaloacetic acid

blocks.prompt: 93 Oxidative decarboxylation of citric acid forms a five-carbon molecule called:
blocks.explanation: Citric acid releases a CO₂ and reduces an NAD⁺, forming five-carbon alpha-ketoglutaric acid.

book_ref.quote: So, a five-carbon molecule called alpha-ketoglutaric acid is formed

blocks.prompt: 94 When succinic acid is oxidized to fumaric acid, the hydrogen acceptor is FAD because:

options.text: the free energy is not enough to reduce NAD⁺

blocks.explanation: When its two hydrogen atoms are removed, the free energy is not enough to reduce NAD⁺, so FAD is reduced to FADH₂.

book_ref.quote: a different electron acceptor i.e., the coenzyme flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) is used

blocks.prompt: 95 Addition of a molecule of water to fumaric acid forms:
blocks.explanation: Water is added to fumaric acid to form malic acid, which is then oxidized to oxaloacetic acid.

book_ref.quote: a molecule of water added to fumaric acid and it is changed to malic acid

blocks.prompt: 96 The electron transport chain of respiration is built in the:
blocks.explanation: The respiratory electron transport chain is built in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

book_ref.quote: The electron transport chain of respiration is built in the inner membrane of the mitochondrion

blocks.prompt: 97 At the start of the respiratory chain, electrons released from NADH are taken up by:
blocks.explanation: NADH is oxidized and its electrons go to coenzyme Q; FADH₂ electrons also go to coenzyme Q.

book_ref.quote: At the start of electron transport chain, NADH is oxidized and the released electrons are taken up by coenzyme Q

blocks.prompt: 98 The final electron acceptor at the bottom end of the respiratory electron transport chain is:
blocks.explanation: Cytochrome a complex passes electrons to an oxygen atom, which joins hydrogen ions to form water.

book_ref.quote: This complex transports electrons to an atom of oxygen that is present at the bottom end of the chain

blocks.prompt: 99 In the mitochondrion, H⁺ ions are pumped by active transport:

options.text: from the inter-membrane space to the matrix
from the matrix to the inter-membrane space
from the stroma to the lumen
from the cytosol to the matrix

blocks.explanation: Energy from electrons pumps H⁺ from the matrix to the inter-membrane space; they diffuse back through ATP synthase.

book_ref.quote: the energy released from the electrons is used for the active transport of H⁺ ions from one side (the matrix of mitochondrion)

blocks.prompt: 100 Oxidation of one NADH (generated inside the mitochondrion) in the electron transport chain produces:
blocks.explanation: One NADH gives three ATP while one FADH₂ gives two ATP.

book_ref.quote: Oxidation of one molecule of NADH in electron transport chain produces three ATP

blocks.prompt: 101 Which statement about substrate-level phosphorylation is correct?

options.text: It needs ATP synthase in a membrane
It makes most of the cell's ATP
It needs no membrane or electron transport chain

blocks.explanation: It is much simpler than chemiosmosis, involves no membrane or ETC, and makes only a small percentage of ATP.

book_ref.quote: Substrate-level phosphorylation is much simpler than chemiosmosis

blocks.prompt: 102 Each NADH produced in glycolysis gives only two ATP in the final balance because:

options.text: one ATP is spent to transport it across the mitochondrial membrane
it is used in the Calvin cycle
it is converted to lactic acid

blocks.explanation: NADH of glycolysis is made in the cytoplasm; carrying it across the mitochondrial membrane costs one ATP per NADH.

book_ref.quote: It costs one ATP molecule per NADH

blocks.prompt: 103 Aerobic oxidation of one glucose molecule gives a net profit of:
blocks.explanation: Aerobic oxidation gives 36 ATP; anaerobic gives 2, so aerobic is 18 times more efficient.

book_ref.quote: In this way, aerobic oxidation of glucose yields a net profit of 36 ATP molecules

blocks.prompt: 104 Aerobic oxidation of glucose is how many times more efficient than anaerobic oxidation?
blocks.explanation: 36 ATP ÷ 2 ATP = 18 times more efficient.

book_ref.quote: Thus, aerobic oxidation is 18 times more efficient than anaerobic

blocks.prompt: 105 Before amino acids can be used as respiratory fuel, they are:
blocks.explanation: Some amino acids are de-aminated and converted to pyruvic acid, acetyl CoA or Krebs cycle acids.

book_ref.quote: Some amino acids are de-aminated (amino group detached)

blocks.prompt: 106 When lipids are used as fuel, glycerol enters respiration as:
blocks.explanation: Glycerol is converted to G3P (a glycolysis intermediate); fatty acids are changed into acetyl CoA.

book_ref.quote: Glycerol is converted to glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate, an intermediate in glycolysis

blocks.prompt: 107 Lipids are excellent cellular fuel because they contain many:
blocks.explanation: Lipids contain many C-H bonds; they are hydrolysed into glycerol and fatty acids before entering respiration.

book_ref.quote: Lipids are excellent cellular fuel because they contain many carbon-hydrogen bonds

blocks.prompt: 108 Which statement about photorespiration is correct?

options.text: It uses oxygen and releases CO₂ but produces no ATP
It releases oxygen and fixes CO₂

blocks.explanation: Photorespiration occurs in green cells in light, needs O₂ and produces CO₂ and H₂O, but no ATP is produced.

book_ref.quote: However, ATP is not produced during photorespiration

blocks.prompt: 109 Photorespiration begins when rubisco adds to RuBP:
blocks.explanation: When CO₂ concentration falls and O₂ is more, rubisco adds O₂ to RuBP instead of CO₂.

book_ref.quote: rubisco adds O₂ in RuBP instead of CO₂

blocks.prompt: 110 When rubisco adds O₂ to RuBP, RuBP breaks into one phosphoglycerate and one:
blocks.explanation: RuBP breaks into one phosphoglycerate and one two-carbon phosphoglycolate.

book_ref.quote: one phosphoglycerate and one phosphoglycolate (a two-carbon molecule)

blocks.prompt: 111 In the peroxisome, conversion of glycolate to glyoxylate produces the toxic substance:
blocks.explanation: Glycolate is metabolized to glyoxylate using O₂; this also produces toxic H₂O₂.

book_ref.quote: This reaction also produces toxic hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂)

blocks.prompt: 112 In the mitochondrion during photorespiration, two molecules of glycine form:
blocks.explanation: Glycine is transported to the mitochondrion, where two glycine form one serine.

book_ref.quote: Here, two molecules of glycine form a molecule of serine

blocks.prompt: 113 In the last step of photorespiration, glycerate moves to the chloroplast and is changed to:

options.text: phosphoglycerate, which can re-enter the Calvin cycle

blocks.explanation: Glycerate is changed to phosphoglycerate (as the book's text says) which re-enters the Calvin cycle.

book_ref.quote: glycerate moves to chloroplast, where it is changed to phosphoglycerate

blocks.prompt: 114 When photorespiration occurs in C-3 plants, they lose:
blocks.explanation: C-3 plants lose between 25% and 50% of their fixed carbon, reducing their yields.

book_ref.quote: they lose between a 25% to 50% of their fixed carbon

blocks.prompt: 115 Photorespiration is a severe problem in tropical climates where the temperature is often above:
blocks.explanation: At higher temperatures rubisco's oxidative activity rises; above 28 °C the problem is severe for yields.

book_ref.quote: At higher temperatures the oxidative activity of rubisco increases than its carbon fixing activity

blocks.prompt: 116 Photorespiration became a problem when free O₂ accumulated and:

options.text: CO₂ and O₂ began competing for the same active site of rubisco

blocks.explanation: When photosynthesis first evolved there was little O₂; later O₂ accumulated and competed with CO₂ for rubisco's active site.

book_ref.quote: competition started between CO₂ and O₂ for the same active site of rubisco

blocks.text: Adaptations to the problems of Photorespiration

blocks.prompt: 117 Which of these is a C-4 plant?
blocks.explanation: Grasses such as corn, sugarcane and sorghum run C-4 photosynthesis; cacti and pineapples perform CAM.

book_ref.quote: Some plants including grasses (corn, sugarcane and sorghum)

blocks.prompt: 118 In C-4 photosynthesis, the first product of CO₂ fixation in mesophyll cells is:
blocks.explanation: CO₂ joins phosphoenol pyruvic acid to form four-carbon oxaloacetic acid; hence the name C-4.

book_ref.quote: It results in the formation of a four-carbon molecule oxaloacetic acid

blocks.prompt: 119 In mesophyll cells of C-4 plants, CO₂ is first attached to:
blocks.explanation: In C-4 photosynthesis CO₂ is attached with the 3-carbon phosphoenol pyruvic acid.

book_ref.quote: CO₂, is attached with a 3-carbon molecule called phosphoenol pyruvic acid

blocks.prompt: 120 In C-4 plants, malic acid is transported from mesophyll cells to:
blocks.explanation: Malic acid moves to an adjacent bundle-sheath cell, where it is broken down to pyruvic acid and CO₂.

book_ref.quote: Malic acid is transported to an adjacent bundle-sheath cell

blocks.prompt: 121 Compared with normal C-3 photosynthesis, the energy cost of making a glucose molecule in C-4 photosynthesis is:
blocks.explanation: The energy cost is almost double, but in hot climates it is the best compromise available.

book_ref.quote: In C-4 photosynthesis, the energy cost for making a glucose molecule is almost double

blocks.prompt: 122 In plants performing CAM, the stomata:

options.text: open during the day and close at night
open at night and close during the day

blocks.explanation: In CAM plants stomata open during the night and close during the day, preventing water loss.

book_ref.quote: In these plants, the stomata open during the night and close during the day

blocks.prompt: 123 CAM, named after the plant family in which it was first discovered, stands for:
blocks.explanation: CAM is crassulacean acid metabolism, after the family Crassulaceae (book correction: the book prints 'Crassulaceal').

book_ref.quote: The name is crassulacean acid metabolism (CAM), after the family Crassulaceae
